Pleasure, this time. I have a house in Bahia, and I try to spend ten days there every month.
Every month? That sounds like an excellent arrangement. What do you do that lets you do that?
Nothing, now. I retired this year, after a long and very demanding career.
I miss the people. I do not miss arriving home at ten at night. Now that I have time, I read the news properly.
What kind of news? I ask because I edit a politics podcast, so it is professional curiosity.
Then we are going to get on well. Current affairs, mostly. American politics, the Middle East, Brazil. Ask me anything.

Hi Braulio, this is Marina from the club. You asked me last week about the activities for the new season, so here they are. On Tuesdays and Thursdays we have the swimming group at seven in the morning. That one is already full, but there is a waiting list. The walking group meets on Saturdays at six thirty, and it is open to everyone. And we are starting something new in September. A discussion group that meets once a month to talk about the news, in English. Fifteen people have signed up so far. I thought of you for that one. Call me back when you can.

Good evening. Here are tonight's headlines. Ministers have agreed on a new housing bill after three weeks of negotiation, and the vote is expected on Thursday. In Washington, the president will meet European leaders on Monday to discuss trade. Closer to home, the city council has approved twelve new cycle lanes, a decision that has already divided opinion. And finally, sport. After a long season, the national team plays its last match on Sunday. The weather, after this.
